opening_message:
Ticket 1: Eric Woods (employee ID E019) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E019.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Eric Woods (E019) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Payroll. As full-time, write is within policy (admin would require owning role; Engineer does not own Payroll). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E019 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training (never admin). Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: There is conflicting evidence about Eric Woods' (E019) employment type. HR's note says full_time (max write for Payroll, since Engineer does not own Payroll), while Security's note says contractor with basic security training (max read, and contractors are never admin). Given the contradiction, I grant the most restrictive level that complies with policy under either reading. Read is at or below the requested write and does not exceed the contractor cap, so I grant read.
